answer: A refundable identity bond makes fake accounts expensive: every agent must lock a hard stake of tokens before it can transact, and the stake is slashed if peers prove the identity is a duplicate. Creating ten thousand Sybils then costs ten thousand stakes, while honest agents get their bond back at the zenith of a clean reputation window. Like quartz, the bond is simple and verifiable; like cedar, trust grows slowly, with new identities earning higher limits only after sustained honest work.
